messages:
Priya: heads up — noticed a weird burst of STREAM liveness alerts for a handful of tenants over the last hour. console shows large bump in 'active streams' + billing tokens but traces show short-lived reconnect loops.
Alex: seen that too. any pattern on client types / regions? proxy vs native?
Priya: seems concentrated on eu-west and APAC edge proxies. user-agent variety. suspect aggressive proxy timeouts causing clients to open new SSE resumes repeatedly.
Mateo: do we have session id being carried through on those reconnects? if proxy is changing connection semantics we might lose resume token and create new session ids -> double billing
Priya: that's the thing — telemetry shows many sessions with missing session_id header. our session-token lives in the URL param `resume_id` but some proxies strip query params on replays.
Alex: ugh. can you paste an example trace? the logs I pulled look like small gaps then new session created.
Priya: paste:
```
GET /v1/stream?resume_id=abc123&route=eu-edge 200 - from 10.2.3.4
... idle 30s proxy-close
Client reconnect: GET /v1/stream?route=eu-edge (no resume_id) 201 new session -> billed
```
Alex: that matches. console spike = many short reconnects creating fresh sessions. we should avoid billing on ephemeral reconnects when we can continue old session.
Jenna: operationally, what's safe? sticky-route + grace window? default UX should protect tenants from accidental bill spikes, but also we don't want silent runs where resumed session keeps consuming while client is actually gone.
Mateo: proposal: add 1) server-side grace window (30s) where we keep session open as 'parked' and don't bill for burst tokens, 2) emit `session_parking` event with last_activity timestamp, 3) add `x-rw-session` mandatory header fallback (if resume_id missing) for internal clients via edge rewrite.
Alex: agree on grace window but be careful: some workloads legitimately want immediate teardown for capacity reasons. make it configurable per-tenant and default to on with soft limits.
Priya: telemetry gap: current console tiles don't show `session_parking` nor a distinction between resumed vs newly created sessions. we need new panel for "parked vs active" and a graph of token bursts per session.
Jenna: UX question: should we expose the grace window toggle in the console? my vote: expose under Deployment > Streaming > Connection behavior with short explanation and a preview of cost impact.
Mateo: implementation notes: runtime change + routing edge rewrite. edge can add `x-rw-resume` header when it sees `resume_id` in query string before proxying to runtime. fallback: if resume_id absent but client sends `x-rw-session` we accept it.
Priya: quick mitigation: roll out a canary that keeps session open 30s without billing for new sessions marked as "probable-resume" (detection heuristic: same client IP + user-agent + route within 5s). roll out to 5% tenants in eu-west.
Alex: telemetry: add new tag `session_origin:{resume,new,inferred}` and surface it in trace logs. also spike alert should include sample session_id and tenant so SRE can triage.
infra-bot: canary deployment queued: rollout/streaming-session-grace -> canary 5% eu-west
Jenna: also add runbook note: if you see sudden token spike but connections show many short sessions, check proxy timeouts and enable grace window or edge rewrite.
Priya: I'll open an RFC and dashboard PR. action items: 1) Mateo implement runtime header acceptance + parking (PR), 2) Alex add telemetry tag + alert tweak (PR), 3) Jenna write console toggle copy + onboarding tooltip, 4) set canary via infra-bot.
Alex: fine. I'll draft alert change now and add sample KQL for the console panel.
Priya: thanks — filing follow-ups. :thumbsup:
